title: 阅读表格填空
goal: 按行列和限定条件提取表格信息。

points.label: 确定表格的对象与比较维度
提取符合行列条件的信息

sources.title: 雅思 IELTS Academic：课表
sources.used: 阅读表格填空的教学内容

body.p: 表格按行列组织信息。行可列出研究方法或历史时期，列可标明比较维度。
每个空格对应一行的对象和一列的属性。对象、数据和条件在原文中常分散在相邻的几句里。

steps.d: 阅读行名与列名。Interview 是方法，Purpose 是比较维度。
先定位这一行的对象，再找这一列要的属性。答案跨句时，核对代词指的是哪个对象。
保留限制信息，例如 only in winter 表示仅限冬季。数字栏同时核对单位。
按题面词数要求提取原词。单位已写在表格中时，填入数字即可。

groups.text:
A research team wished to learn how visitors used a small public garden. The team compared two methods: observation and interviews. Each supplied a different kind of information. The observers could count activities as they happened, while interviews allowed visitors to explain their reasons for choosing particular areas. The researchers planned the work so that neither method would be treated as a complete account of every visitor's experience.

During observation sessions, a researcher sat near the entrance and recorded the number of people using each path. The researcher did not record names. Each session lasted 20 minutes and was repeated at different times of day. Rain was noted in the record because it could affect the number of visitors. The team used the counts to compare the paths, but the figures did not reveal why an individual chose one route over another.

Interviews were held beside the exit. The researcher asked participants about their choice of route and wrote down their explanations. Each interview lasted 10 minutes, and participation was voluntary. The team did not assume that the people who agreed to speak represented every visitor. After collecting the records, researchers grouped similar explanations and compared them with the observations. For example, a frequently used path might also be described as convenient, but the two records alone could not establish that convenience was the cause of every journey along it. Keeping the methods separate helped the team state what each set of evidence could support. Both methods were useful when their different limits were recognised.

Method | Information | Duration (minutes)
Observation | path use counts | (1)
Interview | visitors' (2) | (3)

items.stem: Complete (1) with ONE NUMBER from the passage.
items.why: 依据是 Each session lasted 20 minutes。单位已在表头，只填 20。

items.stem: Complete (2) with ONE WORD from the passage.
items.why: 依据是 asked participants about their choice of route and wrote down their explanations，填 explanations。

items.stem: Complete (3) with ONE NUMBER from the passage.
items.why: Each interview lasted 10 minutes 确定访谈时长。

groups.text:
A museum catalogue describes changes in the containers made by one workshop over several periods. The entries are based on objects that survive in the collection, rather than a complete record of everything the workshop produced. Curators therefore compare features of the surviving examples without assuming that each example represents every object made at that time. The catalogue separates material, decoration and use so that a change in one feature is not mistaken for a change in another.

In the early period, the surviving containers were made of clay. Their surfaces were plain, and several had narrow openings. The catalogue records the narrow openings as a feature of these examples, but it does not say what was kept inside them. In the middle period, glass became the material used in the surviving examples. Some were decorated with lines around the neck, while others had no decoration. The workshop's records for this period do not explain why the two finishes differed.

The later examples were also glass, but several carried a coloured band rather than lines around the neck. A note in the catalogue says that the band was applied only after the container had cooled. The curators distinguish this procedure from the shaping of the container itself. They also record the condition of the surviving objects, including damage that occurred after manufacture. That later damage is not treated as evidence of how the containers were originally made. By keeping these categories separate, the catalogue allows readers to compare the evidence without adding unsupported explanations.

Period | Material | Feature
Early | (1) | plain surface
Middle | glass | some had (2) around the neck
Later | glass | band applied once container had (3)

items.stem: Complete (1) with ONE WORD from the passage.
items.why: 依据是 In the early period, the surviving containers were made of clay，填 clay。

items.stem: Complete (2) with ONE WORD from the passage.
items.why: 依据是中期一段的 Some were decorated with lines around the neck，填 lines。

items.stem: Complete (3) with ONE WORD from the passage. The table entry means the band was applied after the container had _____.
items.why: after the container had cooled 表示冷却后再加色带。
